sections.heading: 2. Core Shona Grammar Rules Consolidated
points: Colours & Describing Objects in Shona ('mutema'): Core Colours: -chena (white), -tema / nhema (black), -tsvuku (red) | Phrase pattern: ruvara rwe-[colour] (e.g., ruvara rwegirinhi)
Talking About the Past ('yakachenuruka'): Recent Today Past: [nda- / wa- / ta- / va-] + verb | Earlier Past: [ndaka- / waka- / taka- / vaka-] + verb
Talking About the Past ('vakawanda'): Recent Today Past: [nda- / wa- / ta- / va-] + verb | Earlier Past: [ndaka- / waka- / taka- / vaka-] + verb
Talking About the Past ('yakasvibira'): Recent Today Past: [nda- / wa- / ta- / va-] + verb | Earlier Past: [ndaka- / waka- / taka- / vaka-] + verb
Talking About the Past ('chakamhara'): Recent Today Past: [nda- / wa- / ta- / va-] + verb | Earlier Past: [ndaka- / waka- / taka- / vaka-] + verb
Shona Greetings & Time of Day ('Manheru'): Morning: Mangwanani | Afternoon: Masikati | Evening: Manheru | How are you?: Makadini? / Wakadii?

sections.heading: 3. Cultural Context & Practical Usage
points: Homestead Garden Tools ('Maturusi') & Local Blacksmith Craftsmanship: Every rural and suburban household in Zimbabwe keeps a set of sturdy hand tools—hoes ('mabadza'), rakes ('mahara'), digging forks ('mafoko'), and shovels ('mafoshoro')—fitted with carved hardwood handles ('mibato yemuti') to prepare vegetable beds and clear stony yard paths..

Veranda Container Gardening & Ornamental Plants in Zimbabwe: Container gardening—planting ornamental foliage and flowers ('maruva') in painted pots and tins ('magaba') arranged along smooth cement verandas ('pamusoro peuriri hwesimende')—is a cherished tradition in Zimbabwean homes, bringing greenery right to the doorstep even during the dry season..

Joina City & the Modern Skyline of Downtown Harare: Completed in 2010 at the intersection of Jason Moyo Avenue and Julius Nyerere Way, Joina City ('chivakwa chihombe cheJoina City') is one of Harare's tallest and busiest commercial and retail landmarks..

Telecommunications Towers ('Mabhusita') Connecting Rural & Urban Zimbabwe: Mobile network base stations—popularly called 'mabhusita' (boosters) in Shona—stand on hills and woodland clearings across Zimbabwe, enabling mobile voice calls and EcoCash digital payments even in remote rural districts..

review_exercises.prompt: Unit 15 Review — Grammar Mastery: How do you say 'Although it rained heavily, we arrived home safely'?
options: Kana mvura ikanaya mangwana, hatisi kuenda kumunda.
Kunyangwe mvura yakanaya zvakanyanya, takasvika kumba zvakanaka.
Mvura iri kunaya kunze saka vana vari mumba.
Zuva rakabuda masikati mbatya dzikaoma nekukurumidza.
review_exercises.correct_answer: Kunyangwe mvura yakanaya zvakanyanya, takasvika kumba zvakanaka.
review_exercises.explanation: 'Kunyangwe' means 'although / even though', 'yakanaya' is past tense ('rained'), and 'takasvika' is 'we arrived'.

review_exercises.prompt: Unit 15 Review — Numbers & Colours: Which phrase means 'three white trucks and two black cars'?
options: rori chena imwe nemotokari tsvuku nhatu
makombi maviri chena nemabhazi mana matema
marori machena matatu nemotokari nhema mbiri
shangu nhema mbiri nehembe tsvuku imwe
review_exercises.correct_answer: marori machena matatu nemotokari nhema mbiri
review_exercises.explanation: 'Marori machena matatu' = 'three white trucks' and 'nemotokari nhema mbiri' = 'and two black cars'.

review_exercises.prompt: Unit 15 Review — Locatives & Existence: Which word means 'Inside the wooden bowl there are roasted caterpillars'?
options: Patafura pane mabhuku nezvinyoreso.
Kumusika kune michero nemiriwo mizhinji.
Parutivi pemugwagwa pane miti mirefu.
Mundiro yemuti mune madora akakangwa.
review_exercises.explanation: 'Mu-' ('inside') + 'ndiro yemuti' ('wooden bowl') pairs with 'mune' ('there is inside').

review_exercises.prompt: Unit 15 Review — Conditionals & Reciprocal Verbs: What does 'tikashanda nesimba tichibatsirana' mean?
options: if we work hard helping one another
when they finished working at the market
because he worked alone in the field
before you start writing the examination
review_exercises.correct_answer: if we work hard helping one another
review_exercises.explanation: 'Tikashanda nesimba' = 'if we work with strength/hard', and 'tichibatsirana' ('-an-' reciprocal suffix) = 'helping each other'.

review_exercises.prompt: Unit 15 Review — Cultural & Historical Vocabulary: What does the phrase 'zvivakwa zvematombo' refer to?
options: wooden handles used on farm hoes and shovels
stone structures / buildings of stone (the origin of the name Zimbabwe)
modern traffic lights at city intersections
plastic tanks mounted beside houses to store water
review_exercises.correct_answer: stone structures / buildings of stone (the origin of the name Zimbabwe)

review_exercises.prompt: Unit 15 Review — Translate this new synthesis sentence into English: 'Vanhu vazhinji vari kutengesa michero nemiriwo pamusika.'
options: Our ancestors built stone walls without mortar long ago.
Two women are sitting under an umbrella near the road.
Many people are selling fruits and vegetables at the market.
We are planning to visit our grandparents next month.
review_exercises.correct_answer: Many people are selling fruits and vegetables at the market.
review_exercises.explanation: 'Vanhu vazhinji' = 'Many people', 'vari kutengesa' = 'are selling', 'michero nemiriwo' = 'fruits and vegetables', 'pamusika' = 'at the market'.
